_note: What a fluency read needs that the passages do not already carry: the prosody scale, the norms, and the wording of the one-minute routine. The passages themselves come from scripts/reading-articles.json, which already holds 600 of them with a measured word count and a Lexile on every one, so nothing here repeats a passage.

routine.d: The student reads from the printed sheet or the screen. Do not read it to them first — this is a cold read unless you are deliberately testing a practiced one.

routine.t: Say the same thing every time
routine.d: "Start at the top and read out loud until I say stop. If you get stuck on a word, I will tell you it. Read it the way you would read it to someone."

routine.t: Start the timer and follow along
routine.d: Mark a word as an error if it is misread, skipped, or the student stalls for more than three seconds. Self-corrections are not errors. Repeats are not errors.
Mark where they got to. Let them finish the sentence if they are close — just do not count past the minute.
How many words they reached, and how many errors. Everything else is arithmetic.
Rate the prosody while it is fresh. A child can hit the rate and still read like a list of words, and that is the part a number will not show you.

prosody.label: How it sounded
prosody.source: Adapted from the NAEP oral reading fluency scale.

levels.d: Mostly in longer, meaningful phrases. Keeps the author's wording. Expression fits the sentence.
Three- or four-word phrases. Some awkward breaks, but the phrasing mostly holds the meaning.
Two- and three-word groups. Some word-by-word. Breaks often fall in the wrong place.
One word at a time. Little or no phrasing, even where the student reads the words correctly.

norms._note: Approximate 50th-percentile words correct per minute. These describe how a large sample of children actually read; they are not a target a particular child owes anybody. A child below the median is not behind by itself — read the accuracy and the prosody alongside the rate.
norms.source: Approximate figures in the range reported by Hasbrouck & Tindal's oral reading fluency norms.

reading._accuracyNote: Under about 95 percent accuracy the passage is too hard to practice fluency on, however fast it was read. Drop to the lower Lexile version before working on rate.
